newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Dispute cancels Greek Cypriot Easter pilgrimage.
newsitem.headline: Dispute cancels Greek Cypriot Easter pilgrimage.

text.p: An Easter pilgrimage by Greek Cypriots to Turkish-held northern Cyprus on Sunday has been cancelled because of terms set by Turkish Cypriot authorities, Greek Cypriot officials said on Friday.
"It is not going to go ahead unless there are some drastic changes," said Takis Christopoulos, presidential commissioner for humanitarian affairs in the Greek Cypriot-led government.
Efforts through the United Nations for the Turkish Cypriots to lift the restrictions failed, Christopoulos added.
A Turkish Cypriot representative said his side did not want the trip cancelled but said Turkish Cypriots were firm that a group of those planning to make the pilgrimage could not do so.
An estimated 600 people were scheduled to travel to the Turkish-held north of the island on a pilgrimage to the monastery of Apostolos Andreas on Sunday for the Greek Orthodox Easter.

It was to be a first such visit since the island's division in 1974 after a Turkish invasion sparked by a brief coup by the military ruling in Greece. More than 2,000 people had initially applied to go.
The pilgrimage was supposed to be in response to a visit by Turkish Cypriot pilgrims to a mosque in the Greek Cypriot populated south last week.
It was one of several planned events over the next few months aimed at promoting goodwill between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities.

"Regretfully Turkish Cypriot authorities allowed themselves to apply certain censorship and crossed out a number of names from the list. This led to the cancellation of the event," said Waldemar Rokoszewski, spokesman for the U.N. peacekeeping force in Cyprus which acted as a go-between in arranging the visit.
Censoring the list of participants was out of the question, he said.
"It is regretful that things developed in this way as the smooth conduct of the event would be beneficial and helpful in the broader sense," Rokoszewski added.

Taner Etkin, who holds the title of foreign minister of the self-styled Turkish Cypriot republic, said Turkish Cypriot authorities were keen that the trip go ahead, but insisted that those excluded would remain excluded.
Etkin said the Turkish Cypriots had objected to eight Greek Cypriots, whom he said were "known as enemies of the Turks, and whose entry to the Turkish Republic of Cyprus has been banned by courts."

"Our doors are open. There are still two days to go before Sunday. This visit can take place within a framework of principles mutually agreed upon by replacing the people in question with others," he told Reuters.
"We have no intention or desire for a cancellation."
Last week some 435 Turkish Cypriots travelled to the southern Greek Cypriot-populated part of the island to celebrate the Eid al-Adha feast at the Hala Sultan mosque at Larnaca.
Rokoszewski said no restrictions were imposed by the Greek Cypriots.
Said Christopoulos: "We never put conditions on them coming and we expected the same treatment. We welcomed them with olive branches."
